answer: One defense is hardware-bound identity: each agent must join through a secure enclave that signs its identity claims, and the ledger allows exactly one trust-wallet per attested enclave key. An attacker spinning up fake agents faces real hardware cost per identity — building a violet-lit rack of chips for every sockpuppet, with the expense piling in shale-like strata like climbing a mesa face. Cloning software identities is free, but only enclave-signed agents earn reputation, so the forgery economy collapses.
